extracted.intended_audience: users of Singular (computational algebraists / mathematicians) using the non-commutative subsystem libraries
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for procedures in Singular's non-commutative subsystem (qmatrix, purityfiltration, nchomolog, ratgb, dmodloc, etc.), describing usage, assumptions, return values, purpose and examples for computing quantum minors, purity filtrations, Ext/Hom presentations, Weyl closures, localizations, and related homological/data operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: qminor
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qminor(I,J,n); I,J intvec, n int. Return: poly, the quantum minor of a generic n*n quantum matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: I is the ordered list of the rows to consider in the minor, J is the ordered list of the columns to consider in the minor, I and J must have the same number of elements, n is the order of the quantum matrix algebra you are working with (quantMat(n)). The base ring should be constructed using quantMat. Example calls shown (e.g., qminor(w,w,3) returns explicit polynomial). See also quantMat.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymGroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: SymGroup(n); n an integer (positive). Return: intmat. Purpose: represent the symmetric group S(n) via integer vectors (permutations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: each row of the output integer matrix is an element of S(n). Example: SymGroup(3) returns rows for (1,2,3),(1,3,2),(3,1,2),(2,1,3),(2,3,1),(3,2,1). See also LengthSym / LengthSymElement.

rubrics_metrics.name: LengthSymElement
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LengthSymElement(v); v intvec. Return: int. Purpose: determine the length of the permutation given by v in some S(n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: v represents an element of S(n); otherwise the output may have no sense. Example: LengthSymElement(1,3,4,2,8,9,6,5,7,10) -> 9.

rubrics_metrics.name: LengthSym
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: LengthSym(M); M an intmat. Return: intvec. Purpose: determine a vector where the i-th element is the length of the permutation given by the i-th row of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: M represents a subset of S(n) (each row must be an element of S(n)); otherwise, the output may have no sense. Example: LengthSym(SymGroup(3)) -> 0,1,2,1,2,3.

rubrics_metrics.name: projectiveDimension
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: projectiveDimension(R,i,j), R matrix representing the Modul M=coker(R) int i, with i=0 or i=1, j a natural number. Return: list T, a projective resolution of M and its projective dimension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: if i=0 (default), T[1] gives a shortest left resolution of M=D^p/D^q(R^t) and T[2] the left projective dimension of M; if i=1, T[1] gives a shortest right resolution of M=D^p/RD^q and T[2] the right projective dimension. In both cases T[1][j] is the (j-1)-th syzygy module of M. Note: algorithm due to A. Quadrat and D. Robertz. Examples include commutative and non-commutative rings; output interpretation and checks (e.g., leftInverse(syz(R))) illustrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: purityFiltration
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: purityFiltration(S), S matrix with entries of an Auslander regular ring D. Return: a list T of two lists, purity filtration of the module M=D^q/D^p(S^t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: T[1] gives a filtration {M_i} of M where the i-th entry of T[1] gives the representation matrix of M_{i-1}; T[2] gives representations of the factor modules (T[2][i] gives repr. matrix for M_{i-1}/M_i). Example usage and printed matrices shown. Assumes base ring is Auslander regular ring D.

rubrics_metrics.name: purityTriang
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: purityTriang(S), S matrix with entries of an Auslander regular ring D. Return: a matrix T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute a triangular block matrix T such that M=D^p/D^q(S^t) is isomorphic to M'=D^{p'}/D^{q}(T^t). Example shows printed triangular block matrix representing coker(R).

rubrics_metrics.name: gradeNumber
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: gradeNumber(R), R matrix representing M=D^p/D^q(R^t) over a ring D. Return: int, grade number of M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes the grade number of M, i.e., the first i with ext^i(M,D) != 0. Returns -1 if M=0. Examples demonstrate outputs and relation to ncExt_R results.

rubrics_metrics.name: showgrades
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: showgrades(T), T list which includes representation matrices of modules. Return: list, grade numbers of the entries in T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes a list L with L[i]=gradenumber(M), M=D^p/D^q T[i]. Example demonstrates that T[i] are pure or zero and printed graded numbers. Input typically T[2] from purityFiltration.

rubrics_metrics.name: allExtOfLeft
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: allExtOfLeft(M). Return: list, entries are ext-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: M presents a left module of finite left projective dimension n. Purpose: For a left module presented by M, compute a list T whose entry T[i+1] is Ext^i_D(M,D) for i=0..n; each entry is a matrix presenting the right module. Examples show printed matrices for T[1], T[2], etc. Note: outputs are right modules (coker(T[i]) are right modules).

rubrics_metrics.name: allExtOfRight
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: allExtOfRight(R), R matrix representing the right Module M=D^q/RD^p over a ring D, M module with finite right projective dimension n. Return: list, entries are ext-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes a list T whose entries are representations of the left modules ext^i(M,D); T[i] gives the repr. matrix of ext^{i-1}(M,D), i=1..n+1. Examples illustrate interpretation and that coker(.T[i]) are left modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: doubleExt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: doubleExt(R,i), R matrix representing the left Module M=D^p/D^q(R^t) over a ring D, int i less or equal the left projective dimension of M. Return: matrix P representing the double ext module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes a matrix P which represents the left module ext^i(ext^i(M,D)). Examples show typical outputs; doubleExt may return identity matrices for trivial cases or nonzero matrices for specific i.

rubrics_metrics.name: allDoubleExt
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: allDoubleExt(R), R matrix representing the left Module M=D^p/D^q(R^t) over a ring D. Return: list T, double indexed, which include all double-ext modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: computes all double ext-modules; T[i][j] gives a representation matrix of ext^{j-1}(ext^{i-1}(M,D)). Examples show how to interpret subblocks T[1][1], T[2][3], etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_pure
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is pure(R), R representing the module M=D^p/D^q(R^t). Return: int, 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: checks pureness of M. Returns 1 if M is pure, or 0 if it’s not. Remark: if M is zero, is_pure returns 1. Examples show both pure and non-pure modules and use of purityFiltration to inspect factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: purelist
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: purelist(T), T list in which the i-th entry R=T[i] represents M=D^p/D^q(R^t). Return: list M, entries of M are 0 or 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: if T[i] is pure, M[i] is 1, else M[i] is 0. Example: after purityFiltration, purelist(T[2]) lists 1's indicating purity of factor modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncExt_R
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ncExt_R(i, M); i int, M module. Compute: a presentation of Ext^i(M',R); for M'=coker(M). Return: right module Ext, a presentation of Ext^i(M',R).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show use in Weyl algebra settings and how to compute double Exts by opposing modules and re-applying ncExt_R to get left modules Ext^i(Ext^i(M,A),A). Outputs are right modules in the opposite algebra; subsequent oppose/oppose conversions used to compare with original M.

rubrics_metrics.name: ncHom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ncHom(M,N); M,N modules. Compute: A presentation of Hom(M',N'), M'=coker(M), N'=coker(N). Return: right module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: M' is a left module, N' is a centralizing bimodule. Note: ncHom(M,N) is a right module, hence a right presentation matrix is returned. Example shows printed matrix output encoding Hom.

rubrics_metrics.name: coHom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: coHom(A,k); A matrix, k int. Purpose: compute the matrix of a homomorphism Hom(R^k,A), where R is the base ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Let A be a matrix defining a map F1->F2 of free R-modules, then the matrix of Hom(R^k,F1)->Hom(R^k,F2) is computed. Both A and Hom(A,R^k) are matrices for either left or right R-module homomorphisms. Example shows explicit expanded matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: contraHom
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: contraHom(A,k); A matrix, k int. Return: matrix. Purpose: compute the matrix of a homomorphism Hom(A,R^k), where R is the base ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Let A be a matrix defining a map F1->F2 of free R-modules, then the matrix of Hom(F2,R^k)->Hom(F1,R^k) is computed. If A is matrix of a left (resp. right) R-module homomorphism, then Hom(A,R^k) is a right (resp. left) R-module homomorphism. Example shows block-structured matrix output.

rubrics_metrics.name: dmodoublext
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dmodoublext(M [,i]); M module, i optional int. Compute: a presentation of Ext^i(Ext^i(M,D),D) for base ring D. Return: left module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: by default, i is set to the integer part of half the number of variables of D. For holonomic modules over the Weyl algebra, the double ext is known to be a holonomic left module. Examples include computing dmodoublext for ideals and modules; printed outputs demonstrate returned operators/generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_cenBimodule
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is cenBimodule(M); M module. Compute: 1, if a module presented by M can be centralizing in the sense of Artin and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: only one condition for centralizing factor module can be checked algorithmically. Example: with makeUsl2() and a central generator p, is_cenBimodule returns 1 for centralizing M and 0 for non-centralizing N.

rubrics_metrics.name: is_cenSubbimodule
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is cenSubbimodule(M); M module. Compute: 1, if a subbimodule generated by the columns of M is centralizing in the sense of Artin and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example usage parallels is_cenBimodule; returns 1 for centralizing subbimodule and 0 otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: ratstd
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ratstd(I, n [,eng]); I an ideal/module, n an integer, eng an optional integer. Return: ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the Groebner basis of I in the Ore localization of the base ring with respect to the subalgebra generated by the first n variables. Assume: variables of base ring are organized in two blocks and the first block of length n contains elements to localize by; base ring ordering must be an antiblock ordering. Notes: output ring C is commutative; polynomial form pGBid and rational/localized form rGBid are provided; during computation the D-dimension of I and the corresponding K(x)-vector space dimension are printed. Optional eng=1 uses slimgb as engine. To see computation steps set printlevel >= 2. Example demonstrates pGBid, rGBid and kbase output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dlocalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Dlocalization(I,f[,k,e]); I ideal, f poly, k,e optional ints. Return: ideal or list, computes an ideal J such that D/J is isomorphic to D/I localized at f as D-modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: base ring is the n-th Weyl algebra over a field of characteristic 0 with standard var ordering x(1..n),D(1..n); assume f does not contain any D(i) and I is holonomic on K^n \ V(f). Remarks: If k<>0, a list [J,m] is returned such that f^m represents the natural map D/I -> D/J; otherwise only J is returned. If e<>0, std is used for Groebner basis computations, otherwise slimgb (default). printlevel controls debug messages. Examples (OTW example) illustrate returned ideal generators and mapping exponent m.

rubrics_metrics.name: WeylClosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: WeylClosure(I); I an ideal. Return: ideal, the Weyl closure of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: base ring is the n-th Weyl algebra W over a field of characteristic 0 and the holonomic rank of W/I is finite. Remarks: Weyl closure is defined as intersection of I regarded in the rational Weyl algebra with the polynomial Weyl algebra. Reference: Tsai, Algorithm 2.2.4. printlevel controls debug output. Example demonstrates computed closure generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: WeylClosure1
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: WeylClosure1(L); L a poly. Return: ideal, the Weyl closure of the principal left ideal generated by L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: base ring is the first Weyl algebra D=K<x,d|dx=xd+1> over characteristic 0. Remarks: definition parallels WeylClosure but for principal left ideal; Reference: Tsai, Algorithm 1.2.4. printlevel controls debug output. Examples show multiple returned closure generators for sample L.

rubrics_metrics.name: holonomicRank
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: holonomicRank(I[,e]); I ideal, e optional int. Return: int, the holonomic rank of I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: base ring is the n-th Weyl algebra over characteristic 0 with standard variable ordering. Remarks: holonomic rank defined as K(x(1..n))-dimension of W/WI where W is rational Weyl algebra; returns -1 if infinite. If e<>0, std used; otherwise slimgb. printlevel controls debugging. Example (OTW) returns rank 1 for given I.

rubrics_metrics.name: DsingularLocus
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: DsingularLocus(I); I ideal. Return: ideal describing the singular locus of the D-module D/I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: base ring is the n-th Weyl algebra over characteristic 0 with standard ordering. Note: printlevel>=1 prints progress messages; >=2 prints all debug messages. Example returns polynomial describing singular locus (e.g., y^2*z^2 - x^3).

rubrics_metrics.name: polSol
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: polSol(I[,w,m]); I ideal, w optional intvec, m optional int. Return: ideal, a basis of the polynomial solutions to the given system of linear PDEs with polynomial coefficients encoded via I.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume: base ring is the n-th Weyl algebra W over a field of characteristic 0 with standard variable ordering and I is holonomic. Remarks and further behavior likely follow standard dmodloc conventions (printlevel, std/slimgb options) — full details continue beyond this chunk. Intended to compute polynomial solution bases when I is holonomic.
